description: Site-wide configuration shared by every tenant. Deliberately unreachable by any customer role: in a multi-company deployment one tenant editing this would change behaviour for all of them. The app reads it through helpers that bypass permissions, so nothing functional depends on a customer being able to open it.

fields.options: The RBI Digital Payments E-mandate Framework governs recurring debits. These values reflect the framework as understood at build time and must be re-verified against current RBI guidance before go-live. See docs/COMPLIANCE_NOTES.md.

fields.description: RBI e-mandate threshold on the TOTAL debit including tax. Above this every debit needs Additional Factor Authentication. The higher one-lakh ceiling covers insurance, mutual funds and card bills only - a SaaS subscription does not qualify.
fields.label: No-AFA Debit Ceiling

fields.description: Registers the mandate maximum above the current debit, so adding users or upgrading does not immediately invalidate it.
fields.label: Mandate Headroom %

fields.description: Mandatory advance notice before any auto-debit. 24 hours is the regulatory minimum and a lower value is refused.
fields.label: Pre-Debit Notice (hours)

fields.description: Required after every collection.

fields.description: On the SaaS subscription supply - unrelated to the tenant's own solar contracts. Confirm with the CA before go-live.

fields.options: The whole payment flow works in tracking mode with this off. Nothing reaches a ledger until it is on and the accounts below are mapped. Same discipline as the Projects tab.

fields.description: Above this a refund needs a billing manager's explicit approval.

fields.options: Provisioning runs privileged operations - creating companies, users and roles - triggered by an inbound webhook. Everything on this tab shapes what a stranger's payment is allowed to build.

An architectural decision, not a toggle. Multi Company is right for the first twenty to fifty tenants and lets you ship; Multi Site is right once one tenant's data loss would end the business, or one tenant's volume degrades everyone else's queries. Changing this is blocked once any Tenant exists - see docs/TENANCY_MODEL.md.

fields.description: Manual Approval queues the job and waits for a human. Worth using for the first few tenants.
fields.label: Mode

fields.options: The last line of defence against one tenant reading another's ledger. It is a gating step: a tenant that fails it is never handed to a customer.
Invitation sending and acceptance are both reachable by people who are not yet your customers. These are the ceilings, per hour.

fields.label: Invitations Sent per Admin per Hour
Acceptance Attempts per IP per Hour

fields.options: This tab decides when a paying customer is warned, restricted or switched off. It ships inert. Dry run is on and automatic suspension is off, so the engine evaluates every subscription every night, writes down what it would have done, and does nothing. Read a cycle or two of those decisions before letting it act.

fields.description: Off deliberately. Watch the engine make correct decisions in report-only mode for a cycle or two before letting it act.
fields.label: Enable Automatic Suspension

fields.description: In dry run the engine computes and logs every decision but performs no access change of any kind.
fields.label: Dry Run

fields.description: Halts every lifecycle state change immediately while evaluation and logging carry on. For use during an incident - see docs/LIFECYCLE_RUNBOOK.md.
fields.label: Kill Switch

fields.description: Comma-separated offsets.
fields.label: Renewal Notices (days before)

fields.options: Two brakes on the same pedal. The circuit breaker stops a bug or a gateway outage from locking out the customer base in one run - a halted run a human investigates is always cheaper than mass suspension. The minimum tenure stops a brand-new tenant being cut off over a first-payment hiccup.

fields.description: Circuit breaker. A run that would suspend more than this halts, performs none of them, and alerts.
fields.label: Max Suspensions per Run

fields.description: A tenant this many days old with no failed payments gets an extra seat immediately and is billed on the next invoice. Conservative on purpose - lower it once you know your customers.
fields.label: Seat Trust Threshold (days)

fields.description: Off by default: a downgrade takes effect at the period boundary and the customer keeps what they paid for. Some clients prefer to be more generous.
fields.label: Refund the Current Period on a Downgrade

fields.description: An internal step somebody chooses to take before a cancellation matures. Never an obstacle the customer has to clear.
fields.label: Offer Retention Step

fields.options: Caps on what an unauthenticated caller can do. Both were added by the Phase 8 audit - see docs/security/FINDINGS.md.

fields.description: The pricing page calls this on every toggle, so the cap is generous. It writes nothing and reads published pricing only.
fields.label: Plan Pricing Calls per IP per Hour

fields.description: A bad-signature request writes a log row. Without a cap an unauthenticated caller could fill the disk with the record of their own attempts. Beyond this, attempts are counted in the file log only - the signal survives, the unbounded growth does not.
fields.label: Unverified Webhook Rows per IP per Hour

fields.options: Every alert below carries an expected frequency at 50 tenants. Anything expected more than about twice a week belongs on a dashboard, not in an on-call channel - see docs/ops/MONITORING.md.

fields.description: Written by every scheduled job. Read by the watchdog, which alerts on absence rather than on error.
fields.label: Job Heartbeats

fields.description: Off until the public funnel is live, or the drought alert fires every week before launch and gets muted.
fields.label: Expect Signups
Health Endpoint Calls per IP per Hour

fields.description: On by default and it should stay on. Impersonating a customer without telling them is a trust violation, whatever the reason.
fields.label: Tell the Tenant About Support Sessions

fields.description: Frappe keeps error logs forever. On this bench that table reached 165 MB - half the database - which hides the signal as well as filling the disk.
fields.label: Error Log Retention (days)
